While I absolutely loved the first Dying Light, its sequel is a buggy, artificially padded disappointment that feels more like an overpriced DLC than a full game. From clunky movement, an awful grappling hook, and bizarrely unbalanced fall damage, to repetitive quests, a generic storyline, and relentless co-op crashes with ray tracing enabled, the entire experience is consistently frustrating. With absurdly punishing trivia quizzes, impossible parkour times, and a total lack of rewarding late-game weapons, Dying Light 2 is a massive downgrade. That being said, this is just my personal experience.
You might be fine if, unlike me, you stick strictly to the main campaign and ignore the side content.

I honestly can't speak on the story too much because I skipped any and all cutscenes after the first couple hours of playing. I think that's a big enough indicator of how much I enjoyed the story in of itself.

The thing is that I really enjoyed most of the combat, and really enjoyed the parkour. I thought the city and map was very well designed. It was really fun figuring out how to traverse the environment to get to where I wanted to go.

Zombies weren't really a problem at all. It's been a while since I played the first game but I recall being out at night scared me quite a bit because it was actually dangerous. But I never had any problems with zombies in this game at all. It seems they put a lot more focus on the human enemies but I don't think I ever got close to dying from enemies. I did die a couple of times from falling to my death though.

I think I would've enjoyed this game significantly more if I could get more immersed into the story and the world itself. Without that it's much harder for this game to really bring me in so I guess it's impressive that they managed to do that somewhat with how good the general gameplay is.

This game is a direct downgrade from Dying Light 2, I preordered it with high expectations. On release u couldnt climb infinitely since climbing was tied to stamina which made no sense since Aiden is superhuman due to experimentation. Also nights had no volatiles roaming on release which was fundamentally flawed. The survivors are so incredibly unlikeable, and most of the characters regardless of faction are unrelatable and two dimensional. Also combat feels limb and weak in comparison to DL1. They addressed this later thank god with some updates and patches but the launch left a bad taste. 

The plot is pretty boring, convoluted, and dragged out and choices have no real meaning expect for a couple which I wont spoil. And exploring was kinda dumbed down since it marked everything on the map if u used ur binoculars, and even then the GRE buildings and GRE anomalies were the only ones worth totally exploring. Don't even get me started on how repetitive the GRE buildings are. I tried to gaslight myself into liking this game (hence my hours) but I really couldn't even after the updates to fix it. 

In summary DL2 Feels soulless and like an artificial playground, there's even huge yellow markers on the buildings telling u where to go like typically AAA slop. In comparison DL1 while not being known for its story, its still widely remembered and has emotional depth. Dl1 had an amazing deeply interconnected map with environmental story telling, and a soundtrack amplifying the atmosphere. I was so incredibly disappointed on release dyling light 2 didn't match the quality they achieved in 2015.

On the bright side the parkour is much better, human combat is actually fun, and there are more side quests than DL1 and a couple of them are really well written and have meaningful choices. Also the game is improving slowly its in a much better state now, most of my criticisms like easy night, limited climbing stamina, and combat have been fixed somewhat. I feel playing Dl1 and DLTB is much more worth ur while u aren't missing on much.

Recommend if you care about gameplay, especially parkour and combat. I enjoyed both. Puzzles with capturing different structures weren't bad, but could be more varied. Most side quests are pretty generic and repetitive with nothing interesting to them outside of like two or three that actually had a pretty good story behind it.

Do not recommend if you care about the main story, which is a disaster. Most characters are insufferable (aside from maybe two) and make little sense in terms of their actions half the time. I kind of liked the way you are supposed to choose between the two factions but only very little of it had any larger impact story wise. That being said, I very much enjoyed that visually and functionally the city transformed based on your actions. Opening up the map and creating safe zones was one of the most enjoyable parts of the game.
With the severe cuts done to the prologue, some characters appear out of nowhere with no emotional impact. Aiden's main motivation is incredibly weak, especially since all you hear from Mia for most of the game is her yelling "Aiden babeiden" which just makes me want to kill her.

Some of the main story scenes and characters will make you want to slam your head into the wall if you care about the narrative at all. Thankfully, the story is a small part of the game and the gameplay does make up for it in my eyes.

I care about the story and the characters if they're good, if not, I can usually suffer through it for the sake of a good gameplay, so overall, I had a good time playing. Especially if I choose to believe that the entire last part was a fever dream. The game puts you back before those events anyway, if you want to keep playing, so it doesn't even matter.

**A Fantastic Open-World Zombie Game with Tons of Fun!**

Dying Light 2 genuinely surprised me in a positive way. The parkour system is especially enjoyable. Running through the city, jumping across rooftops, and dodging zombies just feels incredibly satisfying.

The combat system is also impressive. Melee fights are brutal, the weapons offer plenty of variety, and combining parkour with combat creates some truly awesome moments. Things get even more intense at night, when the atmosphere becomes much more threatening and every mistake can have serious consequences.

The open world offers plenty to explore, tons of side quests, and many ways to develop and improve your character. Visually, the game also looks fantastic.

Of course, not everything is perfect. The story could have been better in certain areas, and some activities become repetitive over time. However, for me, the overall enjoyment of the game easily outweighs these flaws.

**Final Verdict:** If you enjoy zombies, open-world exploration, and action-packed combat, Dying Light 2 is definitely worth playing. It's a game you can easily sink countless hours into. The combination of freedom of movement, atmosphere, and survival elements is what makes Dying Light 2 stand out.

**My Rating: 9/10 – Highly Recommended!**
